Let's simplify the expression by factoring both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x+4)({x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}-5x)}{{x}^{2}+4x} & =\frac{x(x+4)({x}^{2}+3x-5)}{x(x+4)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{x(x+4)}({x}^{2}+3x-5)}{\cancel{x(x+4)}} \\  & ={x}^{2}+3x-5\end{aligned}
$$

Since the denominator is never zero, we conclude that this function has no vertical asymptotes. A plot of the function is below. Note that it is not defined at $x=-4$ and $x=0.$
